rule_name: Banned Constructions, Assert Nothing, Show the Substance
quote: He is very good at it
why: states a ranking/quality verdict about Theo's competence with no measurement or evidence behind it, the same pattern as the banned 'this is the best approach' family
suggestion: Replace with a concrete fact: "His summaries come back with no redlines, and after his eighth month somebody hands him the backlog."

quote: He is very good at it and he is happy, and in his eighth month somebody gives him a stack of old material to summarise because the woman who used to do it retired and it's the kind of job you hand the new analyst.
why: three coordinated "and" clauses of unequal weight (his mood, the plot-relevant handoff, and an aside about job culture) sit side by side with no hierarchy
suggestion: "He is very good at it and happy in the job. In his eighth month, after the woman who used to summarise the old material retires, somebody hands the backlog to the new analyst."

rule_name: Negative Framing and Minimisation, State What a Thing Is
quote: It isn't ruled out. It's just moved to less likely than a company.
why: defines the assessment by denying a reading ("ruled out") that nobody in the scene asserted, instead of stating directly what the revised probability is
suggestion: "The file still lists them, now behind a corporate actor as the likelier explanation."

quote: There was a new teacher for about a day and a half, and there was something wrong with him, and the wrongness was the only thing anybody talked about at lunch for a week.
why: chains a throwaway fact (the teacher's tenure), an ominous one (something wrong), and a consequence (lunchtime talk) as grammatically equal "and" clauses
suggestion: "There was a new teacher for about a day and a half. Something was wrong with him, and the wrongness was all anybody talked about at lunch for a week."

quote: the only thing anybody talked about at lunch for a week
why: a narrator superlative ("the only thing") of the kind the table explicitly bans ("the only time"; "never once") in narration
suggestion: "the wrongness was most of what anybody talked about at lunch for a week"

quote: What he remembers is the feeling that the man was pretending to be somebody, and that all of them clocked it, and that four or five of them started asking questions about him, and that by Thursday he was gone and no adult ever mentioned him again.
why: four "and that" clauses of escalating consequence (a feeling, a shared suspicion, active investigation, disappearance and institutional silence) are strung together with equal grammatical weight
suggestion: "What he remembers is the feeling that the man was pretending to be somebody. All of them clocked it, four or five started asking questions, and by Thursday he was gone."

rule_name: The "Nobody" Construction, Don't Normalise by Reporting an Absent Reaction
quote: no adult ever mentioned him again
why: reports an absent institutional reaction as if it were evidence the incident was quietly ordinary, instead of showing one specific adult's actual behavior
suggestion: "The next teacher never brought him up, and neither did anyone else standing at the front of a room."

quote: One of them wanted to know how the four men would score them. One of them said the response time had been nearly eight minutes and that this was a fail. One of them said repeatedly that running a surprise exercise at four in the morning without putting it on the board was unfair.
why: the frame "One of them" opens three consecutive sentences, the anaphora / three-beat list construction the table says to collapse to one sentence
suggestion: "They argued about how the four men would score them, whether an eight-minute response counted as a fail, and whether an unscheduled 4 a.m. drill was even fair to run."

quote: There is no further entry on file either.
why: stacks a second negative one-line paragraph directly against the first ("There is no reply on file."), restating the same absence rather than the single positive statement the table calls for
suggestion: cut this line and let "There is no reply on file." stand alone as the closing beat

quote: He remembers thinking it was harsh.
why: states the fact that a judgment occurred instead of rendering the judgment itself, the exact shape of the rule's banned example "She thought about that one for a while"
suggestion: "He read the grade sheet on the board like everyone else. Eight minutes, fail, unfair -- harsh, he'd thought, for four kids who'd gone eight-for-eight." or simpler: cut the sentence and let the grade sheet detail stand alone

rule_name: Crutch Phrases That Have Stopped Meaning Anything
quote: sits like that for a while
why: "for a while" is named directly in the rule as a universal duration marker used regardless of what kind of moment is being timed, and it gives no real sense of how long
suggestion: "He puts his hand over his mouth and sits like that until the screen dims."

rule_name: Filtering, Cut "She Sees / Hears / Notices / Knows"
quote: he understands precisely what he is and is not permitted to do
why: routes Theo's grasp of the classification rules through a verb of cognition instead of rendering the constraint itself
suggestion: "every page of it is stamped classified, and the handbook is clear about what happens to an analyst who talks"
